item.description: - **Works with VoiceOver and the keyboard.** The sidebar, tab strip, page bar, command bar, find bar, AI panel, approval cards, settings and the untrusted-certificate warning now have names, states and actions; rows that were only clickable can be pressed from the keyboard and by VoiceOver; status messages (undo, downloads, translation, load errors) are announced. An audit that dumps the app's own accessibility tree found 113 unnamed controls before and none after, and the look is unchanged. (Not yet tried with a real VoiceOver session, so tell me what reads oddly.) - **Reading List.** Save a page for later from Bookmarks › Add to Reading List (⇧⌘D), a tab's menu or a link's menu; the list sits at the top of the bookmarks popover with unread pages in bold, marks pages read when you open them, and comes along when you import from Safari. It is never shown to the AI and never kept from private windows. - **Tracking removed from addresses you open.** Known tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid and the like) are taken out of addresses you type, bookmarks, links you open in a new tab or peek, and what the AI opens. Links you click inside a page are left alone, because rewriting them from outside the engine would weaken sites' cross-site cookie protection. Switch in Settings › Privacy, and per site in the site's settings. - **Prefer secure connections.** An http:// address you open is tried over https first and falls back to http only if the site refuses or drops the connection, never after a certificate error. Switch in Settings › Privacy. - **Clearing site data now really clears your saved sign-ins.** A sign-in snapshot taken a moment before you cleared site data (or removed a profile, or turned "Stay signed in after quitting" off) could still be written afterwards and come back at the next launch. That race, in 0.8.7, is closed, and a test now hammers it.

- **Sign-ins survive quitting.** Many sites keep you signed in with a cookie meant to end when the browser closes, so closing Changmun signed you out of them every time. Those session cookies are now kept, encrypted with a key in your login Keychain, for up to 30 days and put back before your windows open. Settings › Privacy › "Stay signed in after quitting" turns it off (which also deletes them); clearing site data deletes them too, private windows never keep any, and the Agent copy doesn't keep sign-ins. - **Stay open after the last window closes, if you like.** Settings › General › "Quit when the last window is closed" is on, as before; turn it off and Changmun keeps running like Safari, and the Dock icon or ⌘N brings back your last session.

- **Sidebar hidden: the sidebar button no longer crowds the window buttons.** With the sidebar collapsed, its button sat only 8 points from the green window button; it now has the same room as the first tab tile has with the tabs on top.

- **Go on to a site whose certificate can't be verified, as in Safari.** A site with a self-signed certificate, one from a private CA your Mac doesn't trust, an expired one or one for another name now gets a warning drawn by the app itself, with the reason and the certificate's details; "Go Back" is the default, and "Visit This Website" sits under the details and asks for Touch ID or your password. The exception is for that one certificate on that site, lives only until you quit, shows a warning triangle in the address bar and can be taken away in the site's settings. A changed certificate is blocked again. Pages the AI drives never get one, sites that insist on HTTPS (such as .dev and .app) and certificates that went bad since you last visited can't be overridden, and a page you went on to is treated as unverified: no saved-password fill or sign-in, remembered camera, microphone and location permissions ask again, and the AI asks before reading it. - **Client certificates work in more cases.** If none of your certificates match the issuers a site names, you now get the list of all valid ones (with a note) instead of nothing; certificates issued through an intermediate CA are sent with their chain; ones not meant for client use are left out; the chooser no longer cancels itself on the first load or lingers after its tab closes.

- **Signing in to apps through Changmun works.** A sign-in that ends by opening an app (Claude's `claude://`, and others) now asks "… wants to open …" as a sheet, as Safari does, instead of being dropped silently. A page asks at most once until you navigate yourself, a frame inside a page can't ask in the page's name, background tabs and pages the AI drives never ask, and schemes that run automation (Shortcuts and the like) stay blocked. - **AI panel in its own window.** ⌘W and ⌘⇧W close the pop-out (docking the panel back) instead of a browser tab or window, ⌘E closes it from anywhere, other shortcuts go to its browser, questions appear in it rather than in another window's panel, it comes back from the Dock when asked for, and it can show over a full-screen browser. - **Tabs on top.** Renaming with the sidebar overlay open shows one field, not two that cancel each other; closing the overlay ends a rename; Esc closes the overlay; many favorites scroll instead of pushing the tabs out; the mouse wheel scrolls an overflowing strip. - **Renaming.** Folder and bookmark rows don't start dragging while you edit their name; a long folder name isn't cut by just opening the field; Undo restores a bookmark's exact old title; group names have the same length limit as the rest. - **Command bar.** Its suggestions no longer follow the find bar's text, a background tab's title change no longer moves the highlight, and the pointer resting on the list doesn't steal the selection. - **Client certificates.** A request that arrives while the window is minimized is shown when it comes back; tabs waiting for a certificate show a key badge (and the AI panel says so); profile spaces keep their certificate choices to themselves and don't use the Mac-wide preference; a removed smart card's certificate isn't reused; stopping a load drops its request; the sheet waits for you to stop typing. - **Safer approvals.** "Allow" by keyboard or VoiceOver counts only with Full Keyboard Access or an assistive technology on and the button focused long enough; a tab the AI opens is the AI's from its first load. - **Window bar.** A double-click with a tiny tremor still zooms (drags start after 3 points).

- **Client certificates, as in Safari.** When a site asks for a certificate to identify you (a company intranet, a bank), Changmun offers the ones in your Keychain or on a smart card that the site accepts, in the system's own sheet. What you pick is saved as an identity preference for that site (remove it in Keychain Access), so the next visit doesn't ask. Private windows save nothing, and a page the AI is using always asks you: the AI never picks a certificate for you, not even one you chose before.

- **Rename bookmark folders.** Double-click a folder in the sidebar, pinned ones included, or choose Rename… from its menu. Only the name you see changes: the folder stays pinned or open, importing again from the same browser keeps your name, and clearing the name brings the original back. - **Typing Korean (or any input method) in the address bar.** Suggestions now follow what the field shows, the syllable still being composed included, so choosing the first row or pressing Return opens the whole of what you typed, not the part before the last syllable. - **Return opens the highlighted suggestion.** When results arrived after you started typing, Return could open a row from the earlier list instead. - **A click opens the suggestion it went down on,** even if the list changes under the pointer before the button comes up. - **A tab group's header answers a click anywhere along it;** a few narrow spots used to ignore single clicks, which also made double-click renaming unreliable.

- **Rename bookmarks and favorites.** Double-click a bookmark in the sidebar (pinned folders included) or choose Rename… from its menu; a favorite tile renames from its menu. The name is kept, even if you import from that browser again, and Undo brings the old one back. - **Rename a group with a double-click** on its header in the sidebar or its chip in the tab strip. - **A group chip being renamed in the tab strip** no longer hides the first letter behind its dot.

- **Tabs on top, if you like.** Settings › Appearance › Tab Layout now offers On Top: a tab strip above the address bar, with your favorites first as icon-only tiles, then the space's tabs, tab groups as a chip that collapses them, and a + button that stays in view when the tabs overflow. Middle-click closes a tab, dragging reorders, double-clicking renames, and the menus are the sidebar's. The rest of the sidebar opens over the page from the button beside the address bar. The sidebar layout is unchanged and still the default. - **Choose the model and how hard it thinks.** The menu under the AI message box picks the model and an effort level (Auto, Low, Medium, High, Extra High, Max), passed to Claude Code; Auto leaves it to Claude Code. - **Three approval modes.** Ask after reading other sites (the default, as before), Ask before every action (also before typing, choosing or clicking on a page when the chat has read nothing else), or Ask only for actions that can't be undone (the old "off"). Paying, sending, posting, deleting and the like, sign-ins and cookie banners are asked in every mode. Choose from the hand menu under the message box or in Settings › AI; your current setting carries over. - **A + menu and dictation in the message box.** Add Tab…, Attach Screenshot and Add Image… live in one menu, the mic starts macOS dictation, and Stop sits in the box (Esc still stops). - **The panel's head shows the chat.** Its title with a menu of recent chats and Show All Chats, a new-chat button, and a button that pops the panel out into its own window (closing it docks the panel back; the AI's questions come to that window). - **See what it's doing.** "Working for 12 s" with the live steps underneath, cards for the pages that went with your message, and a small ring showing how much of the model's context the chat uses. - **Double-clicking the bar zooms the window again,** following System Settings › Desktop & Dock › "Double-click a window's title bar to".

- **Rename a tab.** Double-click a tab's title in the sidebar, or choose Rename Tab… from its menu, and give it a name of your own. The name stays through new pages, restarts and reopening; Reset Name brings back the page's title. The AI still sees the page's real title next to your name. - **Imported folders keep one name.** Folders brought in from Chrome, Arc or Safari are stored under the same name whatever language your Mac is in, and shown in yours, so importing again after a language change no longer makes a second copy. Folders imported before are renamed once at launch, with a backup kept first, and folders imported twice in two languages are merged. - **Safari's favorites folder** no longer shows as "/ Favorites".
